content: Ligand 1 has neither a terminal methyl nor a pendant saturated ring, so the one-call rebuild is not available here and this will take two cuts. What it does have is a usable skeleton: an anilide at atoms 1 and 18 joining a glycine sulfonamide arm to a 4-fluoroaniline. Step one discards the arm. Atom 1 is the amide carbonyl and atom 2 the methylene, a non-ring bond, so cutting there removes the CH2, the sulfonamide nitrogen, the sulfonyl and the whole chloro-trifluoromethylphenyl - seventeen atoms - and I attach a cyclopropyl to the carbonyl in their place. That leaves the cyclopropanecarboxamide of 4-fluoroaniline, which is the right cap on the wrong aniline; the second step will replace that ring with the meta-substituted one carrying the azine. Two cuts is the cost of a host with no convenient anchor, which is worth remembering when planning a generation-1 rebuild.
